Definition: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of H5869, place of springs); Ænon, a place in Palestine:--Ænon.
BiblicalUsage: Aenon is the place near Salim where John was baptizing, because there was much water there. The place is covered in the Biblical Places collection — this study covers only how the name is used.
TheologicalSignificance: A place name with no sermon attached, and I will not invent one. What it marks is a moment: the last days of John's work, done faithfully in a small place with much water, while the greater ministry rose beside him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
